steps.title: The platform
steps.goal: Can the delivered bytes be trusted, stored without loss, and queried in SQL?

steps.title: The blind target set
steps.goal: Which genes do the child's symptoms alone nominate — a target set chosen with the DNA never read?

steps.title: Discover the alleles from the reads
steps.goal: Which alleles do the raw reads carry in the target set, discovered without the vendor caller — small variants, structural variants, per-exon coverage, and read-backed phase?

steps.title: Alignment-free genotype and copy number
steps.goal: Read without an aligner or a caller, are the discovered alleles at heterozygous multiplicity, is every target-gene exon at two copies, and which public ClinVar P/LP alleles are present at all?

steps.title: Likelihood-ratio ranking over the VCF
steps.goal: Over every protein-coding gene in the VCF, with no hard filter, which biallelic pair has the highest posterior, and what is its P(trans)?

steps.title: Knowledge engine
steps.goal: Does public knowledge — published alleles, case reports, protein-language models — nominate or corroborate a pair for this phenotype?

steps.title: Fusion and unblinding
steps.goal: Fused across steps 2-5 and then unblinded, does iteration 2 rediscover iteration 1's pair, and is a second upload informative?

steps.title: Track 2 enrichment
steps.goal: Which mechanism facts from steps 2-5 and 8 revise the Track 2 card, and what does the drug evidence say for each direction?

steps.title: The mosaic aneuploidy bound
steps.goal: Is mosaic aneuploidy detectable in the sequenced sample with a statistic that has power, and what cell-fraction bound does the data set per chromosome?

hypotheses.statement: The gene carrying the causal compound-heterozygous pair ranks in the top 30 of a phenotype-driven ranking that never reads the callset, the candidate panel, or any variant.
hypotheses.prediction: When the causal gene is confirmed by the oracle, its rank in the proband-only ranking over 5,267 curated genes is 30 or better. BUB1B, the current leading candidate, currently ranks 6.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The oracle confirms a pair in a gene the phenotype ranking places outside the top 200, or in a gene HPO does not curate at all. Either would show the phenotype signal did not carry the answer and that the panel prior was doing the work.

evidence.claim: BUB1B ranks 6 of 5,267 curated genes on the child's seven own HPO terms, scored by a ranker that reads only public ontology files and never the callset or the candidate panel.
Phen2Gene, an independent algorithm on an independent knowledge base, ranks BUB1B 26 of 18,882 genes on the same terms - the top 0.14 percent.

The phenotype ranking reproduces the candidate panel's own confidence ordering without being shown it: the five genes the panel annotates as established rank 6 to 26, while the two it labels case-reports and candidate rank 1,010 and 4,485.

Rhabdomyosarcoma is the rarest of the child's features and drives the top of the ranking; genes matching only nephrocalcinosis also reach the top 20, so a high rank on a seven-term query is not by itself specific.

hypotheses.statement: The parental term HP:0200067 (recurrent spontaneous abortion) degrades the phenotype ranking of the causal gene and should be excluded from the proband's term set.
hypotheses.prediction: Once the causal gene is known, its rank is strictly better in the proband-only ranking than in the with-parental ranking. Measured so far on the candidate panel: every one of the seven curated panel genes rises without the term, BUB1B by 8 places.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The causal gene ranks worse, or unchanged, when the parental term is removed - which would mean the parents' reproductive history carried signal about the child's gene that the child's own features did not.

evidence.claim: Removing the parental term HP:0200067 raises every one of the seven curated candidate-panel genes; BUB1B moves from rank 14 to rank 6.

With the parental term included, four recurrent-miscarriage genes - TOP6BL, ANXA5, ENPP1 and ABCC6 - outrank every candidate-panel gene, showing the term competes with the features that describe the child.

hypotheses.statement: retrospective: filtering the annotated eight-gene MVA panel to alleles that are both rare (gnomAD AF absent or below the recessive cutoff) and protein-altering (VEP impact HIGH or MODERATE) leaves exactly one candidate biallelic set, and it is in BUB1B: one stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic) and one missense allele (absent from gnomAD), both heterozygous, both PASS.
hypotheses.prediction: Re-running the panel filter (methodology 031, table results.panel_candidates) returns exactly two rows flagged rare and protein-altering, both gene BUB1B, both het, both PASS; the ClinVar site-first join (051) finds the stop_gained and nothing else.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A third rare protein-altering PASS allele in any panel gene, a second panel gene with two such alleles, or either BUB1B allele turning out common in gnomAD or homozygous.

evidence.claim: VEP REST over the eight-gene panel annotated 874 of 874 ALT-split alleles; filtering to impact HIGH or MODERATE and gnomAD AF absent or below 0.01 leaves exactly two alleles, both BUB1B, both heterozygous, both PASS: one stop_gained (HIGH, gnomAD AF 3.29e-05, ClinVar pathogenic/likely_pathogenic) and one missense_variant (MODERATE, absent from gnomAD, no ClinVar record).

Site-first ClinVar join: of 2,129 pathogenic/likely-pathogenic ClinVar sites across the panel genes, exactly one is present in the callset - the BUB1B stop_gained, het, PASS, ClinVar condition Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1, two-star review; an independent path from the VEP route (site-first rather than call-first).

Phase is not established by the callset: both alleles are 0/1 calls without shared physical phasing, which is equally consistent with cis and trans; the panel filter therefore identifies a candidate set, not a proven compound heterozygote.

hypotheses.statement: No protein-coding gene outside the eight-gene panel carries a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles that outranks the BUB1B pair: BUB1B is the only gene that is biallelic on PASS calls AND carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele AND sits in the top 30 of the panel-blind phenotype ranking.
hypotheses.prediction: In results.gene_biallelic (every coding allele genome-wide annotated by VEP REST), BUB1B is flagged biallelic_pass with n_plp_pass >= 1 and phenotype_rank <= 30, and no other gene satisfies all three conditions at once. Other genes with biallelic_pass true will exist (recessive carriers of two rare missense alleles are common in any genome) but none will combine a pathogenic ClinVar allele with a phenotype rank in the top 30.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Another gene with biallelic_pass true, at least one ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele, and a phenotype rank of 30 or better; or BUB1B failing to appear as biallelic_pass in the genome-wide table (which would mean the coding-region join or the annotation lost one of its alleles).

evidence.claim: Genome-wide coding scan (38,087 distinct coding alleles, all annotated by VEP REST release 116): 667 genes carry at least one rare protein-altering allele, 65 are biallelic on PASS calls, and exactly one of the 65 carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele - BUB1B, which is also the only biallelic gene with a phenotype rank of 30 or better (rank 6).

Of the 15 biallelic genes carrying a loss-of-function allele, none other than BUB1B has a ClinVar pathogenic allele, and their phenotype ranks are 220 or worse or absent; the biallelic set outside BUB1B is dominated by HLA genes, SERPINA1 and other hypervariable or paralogous loci - the shape of mapping noise and common recessive carrier states, not of a second diagnosis.

The scan covers coding intervals plus an 8 bp splice flank only (1.4 percent of the genome); a deep-intronic, UTR or structural second allele in another gene is outside what this test can see, so the verdict is a statement about the coding fraction.

hypotheses.statement: Among all genes that carry a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles genome-wide, BUB1B is the best-ranked gene in the panel-blind phenotype ranking — the two independent signals (DNA-derived biallelic set, symptom-derived gene rank) converge on one gene.
hypotheses.prediction: Ordering results.gene_biallelic rows with biallelic_pass true by phenotype_rank ascending puts BUB1B first; the second-ranked biallelic gene has a phenotype rank worse than BUB1B's.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A different biallelic_pass gene with a better (smaller) phenotype rank than BUB1B.

evidence.claim: Ordering the 65 biallelic-on-PASS genes by the panel-blind phenotype rank puts BUB1B first at rank 6; the next curated biallelic gene is HSPG2 at rank 150, then PEX5 at 220. Forty-one of the 65 have no HPO curation at all.

The two instruments share no data (the ranking reads ontology files, the scan reads the callset) but the panel that motivated the scan was chosen from the same literature the HPO annotations summarise, so convergence is strong corroboration, not fully independent confirmation.

hypotheses.statement: retrospective: none of the non-PASS calls inside the eight-gene panel is a credible hidden second allele — after VEP annotation, zero are both rare and protein-altering; TRIP13's cluster of filtered calls is a paralogous-read pileup (low allele fraction, all gnomAD-common).
hypotheses.prediction: Re-running methodology 049 over results.panel_suppressed returns 20 non-PASS records, all annotated, 0 flagged rare and protein-altering.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any panel non-PASS allele that is rare and protein-altering.

evidence.claim: All 20 non-PASS records across the eight panel genes were VEP-annotated; zero are both rare and protein-altering. TRIP13's six filtered calls have allele fractions 0.12-0.28 and are all gnomAD-common, the signature of a paralogous-read pileup rather than a suppressed real allele.

TRIP13 is the panel's sole PASS-share outlier (z -4.02 versus chr5), a callability statement: a real TRIP13 allele in low-mappability sequence could be missing from the VCF at every FILTER level, which this test cannot see.

hypotheses.statement: Genome-wide, no gene reaches a biallelic set only by rescuing a suppressed (non-PASS) coding call while also carrying a ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele and a top-30 phenotype rank; in particular BUB1B carries no rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele, so the BUB1B pair does not depend on a filter rescue and no rescued call adds a third BUB1B candidate.
hypotheses.prediction: In results.gene_biallelic, BUB1B has n_nonpass = 0; every gene with biallelic_with_rescue true and biallelic_pass false either lacks a ClinVar pathogenic/LoF allele or has a phenotype rank worse than 30 (or no curation at all).
hypotheses.refuted_by: A rare protein-altering non-PASS coding allele in BUB1B, or a rescue-only biallelic gene with a pathogenic/LoF allele and a phenotype rank of 30 or better.

evidence.claim: BUB1B carries zero rare protein-altering non-PASS coding alleles (n_nonpass = 0); genome-wide, 26 genes become biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued, and none of the 26 carries a ClinVar pathogenic or loss-of-function allele or a phenotype rank of 30 or better.

1,594 of the 38,437 coding rows are non-PASS (MQ40 1,048, QD2 245, LowQual combinations the rest); a real allele the caller never emitted at all - the structural or deep-intronic case - is not a non-PASS call and stays outside this test.

hypotheses.statement: Both BUB1B candidate alleles are single-nucleotide substitutions at bi-allelic sites, so their submission spelling (chromosome, position, REF, ALT) is invariant under bcftools norm (left-alignment and multi-allelic splitting) and an exact-string scorer will match them as the callset spells them.
hypotheses.prediction: For both alleles len(REF) = len(ALT) = 1 and the record carries a single ALT; running bcftools norm -m -both -f <GRCh38 no-chr FASTA> over the BUB1B locus leaves both records byte-identical in CHROM, POS, REF and ALT.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Either allele is an indel or sits in a multi-allelic record, or bcftools norm changes its POS, REF or ALT.

evidence.claim: Both BUB1B candidate records are single-base substitutions with a single ALT, and bcftools norm against the GRCh38 analysis set leaves both identical in CHROM, POS, REF and ALT; genome-wide, normalization changed the spelling of zero bi-allelic records - it only split 66,639 multi-allelic sites (each with two ALTs) and trimmed 39,913 of the alleles that split produced, with zero reference mismatches.
The 43,667 records on hs38d1 decoy contigs have no sequence in the reference used and were excluded; normalization is still a recorded run, not a tested pipeline stage.

hypotheses.statement: The causal compound-heterozygous pair is the BUB1B stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) together with the BUB1B missense allele absent from gnomAD, in trans.
hypotheses.prediction: A submission whose rank-1 row holds exactly these two alleles returns full_match_rank = 1, rank_points = 100 and f_max = 1.0 from the challenge scorer.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The scorer returns no full match for that row. A partial match (partial_match_rank = 1) would mean exactly one of the two alleles is causal and the other is not; no match at all would mean neither is.
hypotheses.path: path 4 — the oracle as a measurement instrument

evidence.claim: The pair is the only candidate biallelic set the genome-wide coding scan leaves standing under the three conditions (biallelic on PASS calls, a ClinVar pathogenic allele, phenotype rank 30 or better): one gene of 65, BUB1B, with these two alleles and no third.

The stop_gained allele is classified pathogenic/likely pathogenic by multiple ClinVar submitters with no conflicts, condition Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1; it truncates BUBR1 in exon 17 of 23, upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain (gnomAD genomes 3.3e-5, exomes 7.9e-5, no homozygote).

The missense allele is absent from gnomAD v4 genomes and exomes, lies in the last exon inside the C-terminal kinase domain (CDD cd14029), and is called likely pathogenic by AlphaMissense (0.92) with CADD 24.5; SpliceAI predicts no splice effect for it, and none for the two rare intronic BUB1B alleles that would be its only in-callset alternatives.

Hanks et al. 2004 established biallelic BUB1B mutations as the cause of MVA with cancer predisposition (Wilms tumour, rhabdomyosarcoma); the reported genotypes combine a truncating allele with a missense allele that leaves residual BubR1, the same shape as this pair - complete loss of BUB1B is embryonic lethal.

Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 showed MVA patient cells carry strongly reduced BUBR1 protein and a weakened spindle assembly checkpoint, with missense alleles acting as hypomorphs - consistent with a kinase-domain missense partnering a null allele.
Rhabdomyosarcoma, the proband's presenting tumour, is a reported malignancy of BUB1B-related MVA (premature chromatid separation syndrome), matching the phenotype prior that favours BUB1B over CEP57.

Phase is not established: the two alleles are 9 exons apart, far beyond the read-backed phasing reach, and no parental samples exist; two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with cis. The trans claim rests on the recessive model and on the absence of any other BUB1B candidate, and is what the oracle will test.

Bulk blood WGS shows no allele-balance or depth signature of mosaic aneuploidy on any autosome; a bulk sample cannot detect an aneuploid fraction below roughly 10-15 percent, so this neither supports nor refutes the diagnosis.

Correction to row 25: the two alleles lie in exons 17 and 23 of the 23-exon MANE transcript (VEP), six exons apart, not nine; the phasing conclusion is unchanged because the distance is tens of kilobases either way.

Oracle reply to submission 1: full match at rank 1, 100 rank points, F-max 1.0 at epcr threshold 0.9963 — the rank-1 row (BUB1B stop_gained + BUB1B missense, compound heterozygous) equals the clinically confirmed answer key exactly; decode table row 1, survivors: stop+missense only

hypotheses.statement: The disease mechanism in this proband is hypomorphic loss of BUB1B function: one null allele (stop_gained, exon 17 of 23) plus one partly functional allele (kinase-domain missense), leaving reduced BubR1 and a leaky spindle assembly checkpoint; there is no gain-of-function or dominant-negative component.
hypotheses.prediction: Public sources agree with the shape: ClinVar and the literature classify BUB1B MVA1 as autosomal recessive loss of function; every reported MVA1 genotype combines a null with a hypomorph or two hypomorphs; no BUB1B variant is annotated dominant or gain-of-function in ClinVar/OMIM; Reactome places BUB1B in the mitotic spindle checkpoint pathway.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any ClinVar or OMIM record of a dominant or gain-of-function BUB1B mechanism, functional evidence that kinase-domain missense alleles act as dominant negatives, or the oracle returning no match for the BUB1B pair (which would make the mechanism argument moot).

evidence.claim: Reactome maps BUB1B (UniProt O60566) to ten pathways, four of them matching the checkpoint/kinetochore/mitotic rule - 'Amplification of signal from unattached kinetochores via a MAD2 inhibitory signal' (R-HSA-141444), 'APC/C:Cdc20 mediated degradation of mitotic proteins' (R-HSA-176409), 'Mitotic Prometaphase' (R-HSA-68877), 'EML4 and NUDC in mitotic spindle formation' (R-HSA-9648025) - placing the gene in the spindle assembly checkpoint as the mechanism claims; the loss-of-function class itself is not tested by this snapshot.

hypotheses.statement: No market-approved drug acts directly on BubR1; approved candidates for this case will come only from pathway neighbours (spindle assembly checkpoint members) and from aneuploidy-stress, proteostasis or tumour-context directions.
hypotheses.prediction: Open Targets knownDrugs for BUB1B, ChEMBL mechanisms for human BUB1B targets and DGIdb interactions for BUB1B return zero molecules with max_phase 4 (approved); approved molecules appear only for other targets in the expanded set (for example AURKB, KIF11, PLK1, TTK, HDAC1-3, HSP90AA1, MTOR, PRKAA1).
hypotheses.refuted_by: Any molecule with an approved status (ChEMBL max_phase 4 or an FDA label) whose recorded mechanism of action names BUB1B/BubR1 as the target.

evidence.claim: In the first mva-drugs snapshot (Open Targets drugAndClinicalCandidates, ChEMBL mechanisms for human BUB1B targets, DGIdb interactions), BUB1B returns zero candidate molecules at any phase, so zero market-approved drugs act directly on BubR1; the 336 distinct approved drugs in the table all attach to other members of the expanded target set (273 targets: 27 seed, 246 Reactome pathway members).

hypotheses.statement: Held-out recall@300 of the phenotype-only ranker is at least 0.90 on the recessive-disease benchmark, so a target set of the top 300 genes is large enough to be worth baiting.
hypotheses.prediction: recall@300 >= 0.90 over the held-out recessive diseases, degraded Zemojtel-style (1-2 terms blurred to a parent, 1-2 noise terms), with a bootstrap interval reported beside it.
hypotheses.refuted_by: recall@300 < 0.90. N is then raised until it is met, before step 2's bait is built, and the raise is recorded.

evidence.claim: Held-out recall@300 is 0.360 (95% bootstrap interval 0.295-0.420) over 200 recessive diseases of the HPO 2026-06-23 corpus, degraded Zemojtel-style; recall@1000 is 0.565 and top-1 is 0.000.
49 of the 200 held-out genes were unrankable: the withheld disease is the only one curating them, so a curation-driven ranker cannot place them at any N.

hypotheses.statement: The blind target set contains at least one gene whose curated disease is a recessive chromosome-instability syndrome.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one target-set gene has an OMIM/HPO-curated recessive disease annotated at or under HP:0002916 (chromosome segregation) or HP:0003220 (chromosome stability).
hypotheses.refuted_by: No target-set gene has such a disease — the symptom ranking and the mechanism-term rule together nominate no chromosome-instability gene.

evidence.claim: 33 genes of the 404-row target set have a curated autosomal-recessive disease annotated at or under HP:0002916 or HP:0003220 (chromosome segregation / stability).

hypotheses.statement: The two independent rankers agree on at least 50% of the top 300 genes.
hypotheses.prediction: The overlap between the local Resnik ranker's top 300 and Phen2Gene's top 300 on the same terms is >= 50%, read against Yuan 2022's measurement of how much two good rankers are expected to disagree.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Overlap < 50% — the ranking is method-dependent, and the target set is reported as one ranker's opinion rather than a converged nomination.

evidence.claim: Phen2Gene and the local Resnik ranker share 97 of their top 300 genes on the proband term set (32.3%); Monarch semsim returns only 50 genes, of which 13 are shared (26.0%).

hypotheses.statement: Fewer than 20% of protein-coding genes have no HPO curation at all.
hypotheses.prediction: The count of protein-coding genes absent from the HPO annotation corpus is < 20% of the protein-coding total.
hypotheses.refuted_by: >= 20% are uncurated — the target set's coverage claim is weakened and the uncurated tier is reported as the larger blind spot it then is.

evidence.claim: 14,523 of 19,723 protein-coding genes in the Ensembl-derived coding regions have no HPO curation at all (73.6%), against the predicted under 20%.

hypotheses.statement: At least one target gene carries a biallelic candidate set in the read-derived calls.
hypotheses.prediction: Enumerating over results.it2_read_alleles gives at least one target gene with two rare heterozygous protein-altering or splice-affecting alleles, or one such allele plus an SV or exon-coverage loss, or one homozygous allele.
hypotheses.refuted_by: No target gene yields any biallelic candidate — the read route nominates nothing and its weight in the step-6 fusion is set from that.

evidence.claim: Four target genes carry two rare protein-altering heterozygous alleles or one homozygous: one core-tier, one mechanism-term, two net. The single core-tier gene is also the only gene among all 792 carrying both a truncating and a ClinVar-flagged allele.

With the read-derived alleles the delivered callset never reported now annotated by VEP, ten target genes carry a biallelic set of rare protein-altering alleles, three of them core tier, up from four genes when only vendor-reported alleles could be scored.

Those 1,199 newly annotated alleles are calls two read-derived callers made on a baited alignment that the vendor's pipeline did not report, and none has been validated, so ten is an upper bound until step 3's alignment-free genotype check runs.

hypotheses.statement: The read-derived DeepVariant calls agree with the delivered VCF at the sites where both call.
hypotheses.prediction: For every target gene, DeepVariant PASS calls agree with the delivered callset at >= 99% of sites where both callers emit a genotype. Computed after the calls exist — a concordance check, never an input to discovery.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Concordance < 99%, in which case every discordant site is listed with its IGV shot and the discovery route is re-examined before anything is concluded from it.

evidence.claim: DeepVariant ships amd64 container images only and the analysis machine is arm64 with no Docker, Podman, Apptainer or conda, so the instrument this claim named cannot run; freebayes and bcftools call -m do run here and are disjoint model classes from each other and from the vendor's Sentieon Haplotyper.

hypotheses.statement: No structural variant confirmed by two method classes removes a coding exon of a gene that also carries a rare heterozygous protein-altering allele.
hypotheses.prediction: No SV called by >= 2 callers of different method classes (read-pair/split-read vs assembly), outside one insert-size of a bait edge, overlaps such an exon.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A DEL or INS does — that gene becomes the lead pair. A DUP or INV does — the gene becomes a lead only once exon coverage or k-mer copy number confirms the dosage change, since Kosugi 2019 puts short-read DUP and INV precision near a coin flip.

evidence.claim: Manta, GRIDSS and LUMPY/smoove ship Linux x86-64 builds only, so the callers this claim named cannot run here; delly (read-pair plus split-read) and dysgu (local assembly plus learned classifier) have arm64 builds and are the two method classes Kosugi 2019 Fig. 6-7 requires.

hypotheses.statement: Read-backed phasing resolves, or explicitly fails to resolve, the configuration of the top candidate pair.
hypotheses.prediction: For the top candidate pair WhatsHap and HapCUT2 either agree on a phase chain closed through the intervening heterozygous SNVs, or report the exact gap that breaks it, with the fraction of the distance covered.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Neither outcome is produced — a tooling failure, re-run before any phase conclusion is drawn.

evidence.claim: Read-backed phasing did not resolve the lead gene's two alleles and the reason is measured, not guessed: they lie 10,911 bp apart with only 4 heterozygous variants between them (mean spacing ~2.7 kb against a ~266 bp fragment), no phase block overlaps the span, and mean depth there is 43.7x so coverage is not the cause.

hypotheses.statement: The matched decoy set yields fewer biallelic candidates per gene than the target set.
hypotheses.prediction: Running every rule of steps 2-3 identically over results.it2_decoys gives a lower per-gene rate of biallelic candidates than over results.it2_targets — the read route's empirical false-lead rate.
hypotheses.refuted_by: As many or more per gene: the read route has no discriminating power of its own and enters the step-6 fusion at reduced weight.

evidence.claim: Target genes yield a biallelic candidate at 4/396 against the decoys' 2/396 — twice the rate — and restricting to genes above half the median bait density does not change it (4/391 vs 2/380).
With four events against two the comparison has almost no power: Fisher one-sided p = 0.343, so a true twofold difference and no difference at all are both consistent with this result.

Without the rarity and consequence filter the decoys yield MORE biallelic genes per gene than the targets (0.573 vs 0.509 core), so the gene selection alone carries no discriminating power — the filter does.

Scoring every read-derived allele rather than only the vendor-reported ones, targets and decoys yield the same per-gene rate of biallelic candidates: 10 of 396 against 10 of 396, Fisher one-sided p = 0.589; on the pre-registered reachable-gene view the decoys are marginally ahead at 9 of 380 against 9 of 391.

The twofold difference reported earlier was an artefact of the scoring join reading only annotations built from the delivered callset, which restricted the enumeration to alleles the vendor had already found and favoured the target set more than the decoy set.

hypotheses.statement: A reference k-mer bait sampled at a fixed stride recovers the reads that carry a known alternate allele inside the baited region.
hypotheses.prediction: For at least 100 heterozygous PASS single-nucleotide alleles drawn by script from the delivered callset inside target-gene intervals, at least 90% of the reads the existing 500-probe strike finds carrying the alternate 31-mer are also present in the bait sweep's survivor set, at stride 16.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Recall below 0.90, in which case the stride is lowered and the pass repeated before any allele discovered by it is interpreted; a recall this low would mean the survivor set is not a superset of the region's variant-carrying reads and every downstream absence would be uninterpretable.

evidence.claim: Of 4,451 reads the 500-probe strike found carrying a witness alternate 31-mer, 4,029 are present in the bait sweep's survivor set: recall 0.9052, just over the 0.90 line.
The per-probe bootstrap interval on that recall is [0.815, 0.974] and only 59% of replicates clear 0.90, so the measurement cannot distinguish 0.85 from 0.95.

Post-hoc: 184 of 195 probes have read counts consistent with a single-copy allele and recall 0.9832 there; the 11 probes found in more reads than one locus can supply recall 0.5312 and carry most of the loss.

hypotheses.statement: The alleles discovered from the reads agree with the delivered callset wherever both call, so a discordant site is a finding about one caller and not about the recovery.
hypotheses.prediction: For every target gene, filter-passing calls from both read-derived callers — freebayes (Bayesian allele-frequency) and bcftools call -m (pileup) — agree with the delivered callset at at least 99% of sites where both emit a genotype. Computed after the calls exist: a concordance check, never an input to discovery.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Concordance below 99%, in which case every discordant site is listed with its evidence shot and the discovery route is re-examined before anything is concluded from it.

evidence.claim: bcftools agrees with the delivered callset at 45,316 of 45,512 co-called substitutions (0.9957) and freebayes at 43,322 of 43,639 (0.9927); at sites the delivered callset marked PASS, 0.9960 and 0.9938.

hypotheses.statement: No structural variant supported by two callers of different method classes, outside the bait-edge zone, removes or duplicates a coding exon of a gene that also carries a rare heterozygous protein-altering allele.
hypotheses.prediction: The merged consensus of a read-pair and split-read caller (delly) with a local-assembly caller (dysgu), after calls within one insert-size of a bait boundary are flagged out, contains no such deletion or insertion overlapping a coding exon of such a gene.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A deletion or insertion does, and that gene becomes the lead pair; a duplication or inversion does, and the gene becomes a lead only when per-exon coverage or k-mer copy number confirms the dosage change, because short-read precision for those two types is close to a coin flip (Kosugi 2019, Table 1).

evidence.claim: Two genes carry a deletion supported by both method classes, outside the bait-edge zone and with over half its span baited, overlapping a coding exon while the gene also holds a rare protein-altering heterozygous allele: one net-tier and one decoy, deletions of 139-1296 bp.
One of the two is a decoy gene, so this signal appears in genes nobody's symptoms nominated at a comparable rate, and both genes are among the most structurally polymorphic in the genome.

hypotheses.statement: Every heterozygous call step 2 made in a reachable target-set gene is called heterozygous by the fitted negative-binomial k-mer genotype model at posterior at least 0.95, with all of its at least three reference/alternate probe pairs agreeing.
hypotheses.prediction: For each such call the fitted model puts posterior >= 0.95 on the het class, and the >= 3 independent probe pairs designed across the variant return the same class.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One or more calls fall below posterior 0.95 or have probes that disagree, in which case each is re-examined as mosaic, as a private neighbouring variant killing a probe, or as a caller artefact.

evidence.claim: Of 518 fully-probed step-2 heterozygous calls in reachable target-set genes, 453 are called heterozygous at posterior >= 0.95 with all three probes agreeing; 38 are contradicted and 11 are no-calls. The claim said every one.
The 87.5% that do agree were typed by an instrument sharing neither the aligner nor the caller, so the agreement is independent corroboration rather than a repeated measurement.

hypotheses.statement: At least one ClinVar pathogenic or likely-pathogenic allele of a target-set gene is present in this sample at heterozygous multiplicity, above the error threshold fitted on the calibration set's homozygous-reference side.
hypotheses.prediction: Counting the alternate k-mers of every public ClinVar P/LP allele in every target gene returns at least one allele whose count exceeds the fitted minimum-count threshold and whose posterior favours the het class.
hypotheses.refuted_by: No ClinVar P/LP allele clears the fitted error threshold, in which case the causal pair, if any, is novel on both sides and no published allele contributes to it.

evidence.claim: Five ClinVar pathogenic or likely-pathogenic alleles of reachable target-set genes are called heterozygous above the fitted error threshold with three agreeing probes. One of them has a balanced alternate fraction of 0.471 and was also called by both read-derived callers.

The other four sit at alternate fractions of 0.061 to 0.091, about a tenth of a heterozygote, and no caller reported any of them. The fitted error rate of 0.000247 makes any alternate count of two or more improbable under homozygous reference, so the model calls them heterozygous; they are better read as the error model being too tight than as presence.

hypotheses.statement: No exon of a reachable target-set gene, nor any such gene pooled, falls below the 2.5th percentile of a 1,000-exon null copy-number band measured on this sample.
hypotheses.prediction: Alignment-free copy number, computed against a local flanking denominator and reported with its surviving unique-k-mer count, leaves every measured target exon or pooled gene inside the null band.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One falls below the 2.5th percentile, which makes it a deletion candidate for step 6 after checking which side of the baited-span and minimum-length controls any contradicting structural-variant call sits on.

evidence.claim: One exon of a reachable net-tier target gene, BRD4 exon 7, reads at copy number 0.85 against a null-band lower edge of 1.028, on 573 surviving unique k-mers.

No core or mechanism-term autosomal region falls below the band, and those are the two tiers with both denominators available: all 102 core and all 132 mechanism-term regions have a local flanking denominator as well as the genome-wide one.

38 of the 45 below-band regions are on chromosome X, across 21 genes, and the proband is male: X regions read at a median copy number of 0.95 against 2.00 on the autosomes. Nothing told the measurement which chromosome anything was on, so this is a positive control rather than a finding.

Four of the seven autosomal below-band rows have 0 to 242 surviving k-mers and were already excluded by the stage-0 reachability gate. A copy number computed over no surviving k-mers is an absence of measurement, not a measurement of absence.

hypotheses.statement: At least 80 percent of the 1,199 alleles the delivered callset never reported, which step 2's read-derived callers found and annotated, are confirmed at the same multiplicity by alignment-free k-mer genotyping.
hypotheses.prediction: Of the 1,199 alleles in warehouse.it2_read_annotations that receive at least three usable probe pairs, at least 80 percent are called at the same genotype class the read callers assigned, at posterior >= 0.95.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Fewer than 80 percent are confirmed, in which case every biallelic count step 2 reported is revised downward and the read route gains a measured false-positive rate in place of a caveat.

evidence.claim: Of the 1,199 alleles the delivered callset never reported, the fully-probed ones are confirmed at the same multiplicity by k-mer genotype in only 27% to 43% per tier, against the 80% the claim named.

The same instrument confirms 91% to 97% of the alleles the delivered callset did report, in the same genes and in the same run, so the low rate on the vendor-unreported set is a property of those alleles and not of the instrument.

hypotheses.statement: Both alleles of the top-ranked biallelic candidate pair step 2 discovered are present at one-copy multiplicity, at posterior at least 0.95 each.
hypotheses.prediction: The k-mer genotype of each of the two alleles puts posterior >= 0.95 on the heterozygous class, so each allele sits on one of the two copies rather than on both or on neither.
hypotheses.refuted_by: Either allele is not called single-copy at that posterior. This is a dosage statement and is not evidence of trans either way: read-backed phasing of this pair is impossible and no population statistic replaces it.
hypotheses.path: iteration2 step-3 README 5, adopted by plan 11.4

evidence.claim: Both alleles of the top-ranked biallelic candidate pair are called heterozygous at posterior 1.0 with all three probes agreeing, at counts of 11 reference to 12 alternate and 18 to 16 — one copy each, by an instrument with no aligner and no caller in the chain.

hypotheses.statement: Genes whose surviving-k-mer bait density is below half the median yield no confident k-mer genotype.
hypotheses.prediction: Every allele in a gene flagged unreachable by the stage-0 reachability rule returns a no-call, or a posterior below 0.95, or fewer than three usable probe pairs.
hypotheses.refuted_by: A gene below half the median bait density yields a confident genotype at posterior >= 0.95 with three agreeing probes, in which case the reachability limit is weaker than claimed and the rule is reported as conservative.
hypotheses.path: iteration2 step-3 README 5, adopted by plan 11.4

evidence.claim: The 21 genes the stage-0 reachability rule excluded yield 215 confident calls across 1,222 alleles, a 17.6% rate rather than none.
Reachable genes yield a confident call for 59.6% of their alleles, so the gate is 3.4 times enriched for callable alleles even though it is not absolute.

hypotheses.statement: The top-posterior biallelic pair genome-wide, scored by the step-4 likelihood ratio with no hard filter, sits in a gene of the step-1 blind target set.
hypotheses.prediction: Ranking every gene in the callset by pair posterior, the rank-1 pair's gene carries tier core, mechanism-term or net in results.it2_targets.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The rank-1 pair's gene is absent from results.it2_targets: the symptom-derived target set was too small, and step 2's discovery is re-run on that gene.

evidence.claim: Scored genome-wide with no hard filter over 11,465 genes and 51,920 biallelic hypotheses, the top-ranked gene is BUB1B, which carries tier core in results.it2_targets.
The phenotype lane contributes x52.08 of the leader's ratio, so the ranking and the target set are not independent routes; the leader's genotype-only ratio is 6,548.

With the phenotype lane ablated, the DNA alone puts BUB1B joint third at 6,548 behind ADAMTS1 (529,850), HLA-DRB1 (29,451) and HLA-DQA1; the support is for the combination of the two routes, not for the genotype route alone.

hypotheses.statement: The runner-up gene's best pair posterior is at least one order of magnitude below the leading gene's.
hypotheses.prediction: posterior(best pair of gene rank 1) / posterior(best pair of gene rank 2) >= 10.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The ratio is below 10: the ranking does not separate a single lead, and two leads are carried into step 6.

evidence.claim: The runner-up gene ADAMTS1 sits 1.70x behind BUB1B, well inside the one order of magnitude the claim required.
The runner-up's pair is phased cis by the caller's own physical phasing, so it leaves one intact copy; 1,191 of 35,120 compound hypotheses are cis.

hypotheses.statement: No gene that can only be scored through the network-proximity lane - no HPO curation of its own - reaches the top 20 by pair posterior.
hypotheses.prediction: Every gene in the top 20 by pair posterior carries a phenotype score in warehouse.hpo_gene_scores; the count entering solely via the STRING proximity lane is zero.
hypotheses.refuted_by: At least one top-20 gene has no phenotype score and entered through the network lane alone: the lane is evidence rather than a tie-break, and the report says so.
hypotheses.path: step-4 network-proximity lane (substitute for plan H022, no Exomiser reference run)

evidence.claim: ADAMTS1 has no curated phenotype and reached rank 2 genome-wide, so not every top-20 gene carries a phenotype score.
No gene in the top 25 entered through the network-proximity lane, so the stated mechanism of refutation did not occur.

hypotheses.statement: Under a phenotype-permutation null, fewer than 1 in 1,000 random seven-term sets drawn with the child's term-depth profile produce a top pair posterior at or above the observed one.
hypotheses.prediction: Recomputing the whole ranking for each of 1,000 permuted term sets, the count of draws whose top posterior >= the observed top posterior is 0, giving an empirical p < 0.001.
hypotheses.refuted_by: One or more of the 1,000 draws reaches the observed top posterior: the lead is not phenotype-specific and is reported as a ranking a random symptom set could also produce.

evidence.claim: 55 of 1,000 permuted seven-term sets reached or exceeded the observed top ratio, giving an empirical p of 0.056 against the pre-registered threshold of 0.001.

The null is nearly degenerate: 945 of 1,000 draws report the same top value, produced by an uncurated gene no term permutation can move, and every exceeding draw is HLA-DRB1 promoted into a better rank band.

hypotheses.statement: Under the identical likelihood ratio, the step-1 target genes separate from their matched decoys: the bootstrap interval of the target-versus-decoy AUC on best-pair posterior excludes 0.5.
hypotheses.prediction: AUC of target best-pair posteriors against decoy best-pair posteriors is above 0.5 with a 95 percent bootstrap interval whose lower bound is above 0.5.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The interval covers 0.5: the likelihood ratio has no measured discrimination between a symptom-nominated gene and a size-matched control, and the step reports that instead of a lead.
hypotheses.path: step-4 decoy null (finding F4, plan section 11.5)

evidence.claim: Target genes separate from their size-matched decoys at AUC 0.706 with a 95 percent bootstrap interval of [0.655, 0.751] over 256 targets and 266 decoys, so the interval excludes 0.5.

Step 2 measured the same two sets as indistinguishable before any filter (10 of 396 each, Fisher one-sided p = 0.589), so the separation measured here was produced by the scoring and not by the gene list.

hypotheses.statement: P(trans) for the leading pair is undetermined: at least one of its two alleles is absent from the gnomAD v2 exome co-occurrence dataset, so no observed compound-heterozygosity probability exists for it.
hypotheses.prediction: Resolving both alleles to gnomAD v2 identifiers and querying variant_cooccurrence returns no record for the pair; the pair is reported with the published rare-pair base rate and the state undetermined.
hypotheses.refuted_by: gnomAD returns a p_compound_heterozygous for the pair: an observed population co-occurrence estimate exists and is quoted with its caveat instead of the base rate.

evidence.claim: gnomAD v2 returned no co-occurrence estimate for any of the 25 leading pairs; only 5 of their 50 alleles resolve in that dataset, and the lead pair's second allele carries no dbSNP identifier.

hypotheses.statement: At least one published allele - reported in ClinVar as pathogenic or likely pathogenic, or carrying at least one publication in LitVar - is present in this child at heterozygous or homozygous-alternate multiplicity in a gene that step 4 ranks in its top 20.
hypotheses.prediction: The catalogue join against results.it2_kmer_genotypes (origin clinvar) and against the LitVar publication counts of the child own alleles returns at least one row whose gene is in the step-4 top 20 and whose k-mer call is het or hom-alt.
hypotheses.refuted_by: No published allele of any step-4 top-20 gene is present in the child: every such allele is hom-ref or no-call. The leading pair would then be novel on both sides, and the knowledge route would contribute no allele-level corroboration.

evidence.claim: The step-4 leading gene carries a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic truncating allele with 4 LitVar publications, and the k-mer route independently types a ClinVar pathogenic allele in the same gene at heterozygous multiplicity, posterior 1.0, 3 of 3 probes agreeing.
1,821 of 1,914 askable alleles carry at least one LitVar publication, so the published-allele column is saturated at 95.1 percent and orders almost nothing on its own.
The leading pair missense partner has no dbSNP identifier, so LitVar could not be asked about it; the pair is one published allele and one no literature index has seen.

hypotheses.statement: At least one published case report matches five or more of the child seven proband HPO terms and names a gene that step 4 ranks in its top 20.
hypotheses.prediction: In the script-derived anchor table, at least one PMID is returned by five or more of the seven per-term PubTator queries for a single step-4 top-20 gene.
hypotheses.refuted_by: No PMID reaches five matched terms for any top-20 gene. The literature then corroborates no lead at case-report level, and step 6 records the knowledge route as silent rather than negative.

hypotheses.statement: The knowledge score separates the 404 symptom-nominated target genes from the 396 matched decoy genes.
hypotheses.prediction: The target-versus-decoy AUC of the knowledge score, with a bootstrap interval computed the same way step 4 computed its own, has an interval that excludes 0.5.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The bootstrap interval covers 0.5. The knowledge route then has no measured discriminating power and enters step 6 as a confirmation route at weight zero, exactly as the read route did when H020 was refuted.

hypotheses.statement: The knowledge ranking reorders the leading genes against a baseline that ranks them by PubMed hit count alone.
hypotheses.prediction: Spearman rank correlation between the knowledge ranking and the PubMed-count ranking is below 0.9, or the two top-5 sets differ by at least one gene.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The correlation is 0.9 or above and the two top-5 sets are identical. The knowledge route is then citation volume under another name, is reported as a negative result, and is dropped from the step-6 fusion.

hypotheses.statement: The missense allele of the leading pair falls inside an annotated InterPro domain, in a region the structure model is confident about, and the AlphaMissense class agrees that it is damaging.
hypotheses.prediction: The residue maps inside at least one InterPro domain range of the gene canonical UniProt entry, the AlphaFold per-residue pLDDT at that position is 70 or above, and the AlphaMissense class recorded for the allele is likely_pathogenic.
hypotheses.refuted_by: The residue falls outside every annotated domain, or the pLDDT is below 70 so the model has no confident opinion there, or AlphaMissense does not call it likely_pathogenic. Any one of the three refutes the claim and is reported separately.

evidence.claim: The leading missense residue is outside every InterPro entry typed domain, sitting at 95.4 percent along the protein, past both the domain-typed entry and the protein-kinase-like superfamily entry.
AlphaFold per-residue pLDDT at that residue is 91.06, so the structure model is confident about the region rather than silent on it.
AlphaMissense calls the allele likely_pathogenic, agreeing with the step-4 lane that scored it.
The residue is inside an InterPro family entry spanning 2 to 98.7 percent of the protein, which is why family and superfamily entry types are excluded from the domain test.
